import numpy as np, pandas as pd
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
n = 2000
k = rng.integers(0, 4, n)
centers = rng.normal(0, 5, (4, 20))
df = pd.DataFrame(centers[k] + rng.normal(0, 1, (n, 20)), columns=[f'x{i}' for i in range(20)])
df['group'] = [f'g{v}' for v in k]

steps.name: set title and subtitle
steps.eval: a.titleOverlay = { ...a.titleOverlay, title: 'My Test Map', subtitle: 'A subtitle here', fontSize: 28, color: '#ff9900' }

steps.name: PNG title area contains non-background pixels (orange text rendered)
steps.eval: (() => { const img = new Image(); img.onload = () => { const c = document.createElement('canvas'); c.width = img.width; c.height = img.height; const g = c.getContext('2d'); g.drawImage(img, 0, 0); const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1; const scanW = Math.round(200 * dpr); const scanH = Math.round(60 * dpr); const pxData = g.getImageData(Math.round(10 * dpr), Math.round(30 * dpr), scanW, scanH).data; let orangePixels = 0; for (let i = 0; i < pxData.length; i += 4) { if (pxData[i] > 180 && pxData[i+1] > 100 && pxData[i+1] < 180 && pxData[i+2] < 60) orangePixels++; } window.__titlePxCheck = { ok: orangePixels > 10, orangePixels }; }; img.src = h.png; })()
